faq.q: Can a foreign company own 100% of an Indian subsidiary?
faq.a: In many sectors, yes, under the automatic route. Whether 100% ownership is permitted, and whether government approval is needed, depends on the sector, the investor's country, beneficial ownership and India's FDI policy. Investors from countries that share a land border with India need prior government approval. We confirm the applicable route before incorporation.

faq.q: Should we set up a subsidiary, LLP, branch office or liaison office?
faq.a: It depends on what you plan to do in India. A subsidiary can carry on most business activities. A liaison office can only undertake representative activities and cannot earn income, while branch and project offices have defined permitted activities and need approval through an authorised bank. We recommend the structure after understanding your activities, ownership and plans.

faq.q: How long does it take to incorporate an Indian company?
faq.a: Typically two to three weeks once complete, correctly executed documents are available. Preparing, notarising and apostilling documents abroad often takes longer than the filing itself, so we start with a clear document checklist.

faq.q: Can the entire incorporation be completed remotely?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Foreign shareholders and directors sign documents in their own country, have them notarised and apostilled, and courier or share them with us. Digital signatures are obtained online with verification. You do not need to travel to India to incorporate.

faq.q: What documents do foreign shareholders and directors need to provide?
faq.a: Typically a passport and recent address proof for individuals, and incorporation documents, a board resolution and beneficial ownership details for a corporate shareholder. Documents executed outside India usually need notarisation and an apostille. We share an exact checklist for your structure.

faq.q: Is an Indian resident director mandatory?
faq.a: Yes, for a company. Section 149(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires at least one director who has stayed in India for 182 days or more during the financial year. For a newly incorporated company the requirement applies proportionately. We can propose a resident director, subject to eligibility, due diligence, consent and agreed responsibilities.

faq.q: How do we fund the Indian subsidiary and report the investment?
faq.a: Share capital is remitted from abroad into the company's Indian bank account through banking channels, and shares are issued in line with the pricing rules. The company then reports the allotment to the RBI in Form FC-GPR within 30 days. Later transfers of shares between residents and non-residents are reported in Form FC-TRS.

faq.q: How long does it take to open a corporate bank account?
faq.a: Usually one to three weeks after incorporation, depending on the bank and its KYC review of foreign shareholders, directors and beneficial owners. We prepare the documentation and coordinate with the bank, but approval rests with the bank.

faq.q: Can we start operations immediately after incorporation?
faq.a: Not always. Incorporation creates the company, but it also needs a bank account, receipt of share capital, a declaration of commencement of business filed within 180 days, and any registrations its activities require, such as GST. We plan these steps so you know when the entity can actually begin trading.

faq.q: What are the annual compliance and audit obligations?
faq.a: Typically board and shareholder meetings, statutory registers, annual MCA filings, statutory audit by an independent auditor, income-tax returns, and GST and TDS returns where registered. FEMA filings such as the annual FLA return apply where the entity has foreign investment. We set up a compliance calendar for your entity.

faq.q: Can GAA manage our accounting, payroll, tax and secretarial compliance after incorporation?
faq.a: Yes. Through our India Operations engagement we manage accounting, payroll, tax compliance, audit coordination and secretarial compliance under one team, with regular reporting to your head office. You can also engage us for specific services only.

faq.q: Do you advise private, public and listed companies?
faq.a: Yes. We advise private and public companies, LLPs and their promoters and boards on company law and governance. For listed companies and regulated entities such as NBFCs, we advise on the company law and governance aspects, with securities-market or sector-specific matters scoped to the applicable requirements.

faq.q: What is the difference between a secretarial audit and a compliance review?
faq.a: A secretarial audit under Section 204 of the Companies Act, 2013 is mandatory for listed companies and certain larger public companies and companies with significant borrowings. It is carried out by a practising company secretary and reported in Form MR-3. A voluntary compliance review is an internal health check for any company. Remediation support is engaged separately from an audit so that the audit stays independent.

faq.q: Can you take care of our annual ROC filings?
faq.a: Yes. We prepare and file the annual return and financial statement forms with the Registrar of Companies and track event-based filings during the year. The company's board remains responsible for approving the financial statements, the statutory auditor for the audit, and the company for the accuracy of its disclosures.

faq.q: What approvals are needed to issue shares to new investors?
faq.a: Typically board approval, a special resolution of shareholders for a private placement or preferential allotment, a valuation report where required, an offer letter and the return of allotment filed within the prescribed time. Where the investor is non-resident, FEMA pricing rules and RBI reporting also apply. The exact route depends on the type of issue.

faq.q: Can a loan be converted into equity?
faq.a: Often, yes. Where the loan terms include a conversion option approved by special resolution before the loan was taken, conversion follows that route. Otherwise conversion is usually done as a fresh allotment with the related approvals. Loans from non-residents also need to meet FEMA requirements. We assess the available route for your loan.

faq.q: Can we restructure shareholding without transferring business assets?
faq.a: In many cases, yes, through share transfers, fresh issues, buybacks or a holding structure, depending on your objective. Each option has different company law, tax, stamp duty and FEMA implications, which we set out before you decide.

faq.q: Can you review a shareholders' agreement or share purchase agreement?
faq.a: Yes. We review investment and transaction agreements for company law and governance consistency, including whether the articles need amendment to reflect investor rights. Commercial negotiation and specialist legal drafting are handled with legal counsel where the engagement requires.

faq.q: What should a company do after receiving an ROC notice?
faq.a: Do not ignore it. Note the response deadline, collect the records the notice refers to and take advice before replying. Depending on the issue, the right response may be an explanation, rectification of the default, a compounding application or an adjudication process. We can review the notice and prepare the response.

faq.q: What is the difference between compounding and adjudication?
faq.a: Compounding under Section 441 applies to certain offences: the company or officer applies to settle the offence by paying a compounding fee. Adjudication under Section 454 applies to defaults that carry a monetary penalty, which an adjudicating officer imposes after a hearing. Which applies depends on the provision breached.

faq.q: Can you undertake secretarial due diligence before an investment?
faq.a: Yes. We review the company's incorporation records, capital history, statutory registers, filings and approvals, and report gaps, risks and recommended corrective actions before you invest or acquire.

faq.q: Can we engage you for a single matter?
faq.a: Yes. You can engage us for a single opinion or corporate action, an ongoing advisory retainer or an independent governance review.

faq.q: What does corporate and secretarial due diligence cover?
faq.a: Our review examines incorporation records, constitutional documents, shareholding history, statutory registers, MCA filings, board and shareholder approvals, governance records and other agreed corporate documents. We provide a findings report highlighting identified gaps, risks and recommended corrective actions. Tax, litigation, intellectual property and other specialist reviews may be undertaken separately.

faq.q: Do you support mergers and demergers under the Companies Act?
faq.a: Yes. We support the corporate and regulatory aspects of mergers, amalgamations and demergers, including transaction planning, scheme-related documentation, approval coordination, applicable statutory procedures, filings and post-transaction compliance. The process depends on the transaction structure and applicable legal route.

faq.q: Can GAA assist with transactions involving foreign investors?
faq.a: Yes. We advise on applicable FEMA and foreign investment requirements, including entry routes, sectoral conditions, pricing guidelines, corporate approvals and reporting obligations for investments and share transfers involving non-residents.

faq.q: Does GAA prepare transaction documentation?
faq.a: We prepare and coordinate corporate resolutions, approvals, transaction checklists, closing records and agreed transaction documentation. Depending on the nature of the assignment, specialist legal counsel may be involved in contractual drafting, negotiation and legal review.

faq.q: Can we engage GAA only for due diligence?
faq.a: Yes. You may engage us for corporate and secretarial due diligence, a specific transaction stage or a coordinated transaction mandate. The scope, deliverables, timelines and professional fees are agreed before commencement.

faq.q: Can GAA assist with private placements and investment rounds?
faq.a: Yes. We support applicable corporate and regulatory requirements for equity investments, including private placements, preferential allotments, rights issues, convertible instruments, corporate approvals, statutory filings and FEMA reporting where applicable.

faq.q: How long does corporate due diligence take?
faq.a: The timeline depends on the company's size, corporate history, volume of records, review scope and availability of documents. Following an initial assessment, we provide an indicative work plan and expected completion schedule.

faq.q: What is the difference between a share acquisition and a business transfer?
faq.a: A share acquisition involves acquiring ownership interests in a company, whereas a business transfer involves transferring an identified business or undertaking under an agreed structure. The legal, tax, contractual, regulatory and approval implications differ. The appropriate approach depends on the transaction objectives and circumstances.

faq.q: What happens between signing and closing?
faq.a: Depending on the transaction, this stage may involve satisfying conditions precedent, obtaining approvals, completing documentation, resolving diligence findings, coordinating consideration and confirming closing deliverables. GAA supports the agreed corporate and regulatory components of this process.

faq.q: What support is available after transaction closing?
faq.a: We assist with applicable statutory filings, updates to registers and corporate records, board and shareholder changes, FEMA reporting and continuing governance or compliance requirements. Ongoing services may be provided under a separate engagement.

faq.q: What net owned fund is needed to register an NBFC?
faq.a: The RBI prescribes a minimum net owned fund for each category of NBFC, and these requirements have been revised under the scale-based regulatory framework. We confirm the current requirement for your proposed category before you apply.

faq.q: How long does NBFC registration take?
faq.a: It depends on the completeness of the application and the RBI’s review. We prepare a complete application and help you respond to any queries to avoid delays.

faq.q: Does a change in shareholding need RBI approval?
faq.a: Prior RBI approval is generally needed for a change in control, for acquisitions of shareholding above the thresholds the RBI specifies, and for certain changes in management. We assess whether approval is needed and handle the application.

faq.q: Which returns does an NBFC need to file with the RBI?
faq.a: This depends on the NBFC’s category, size and activities. We map the returns that apply to you and maintain a filing calendar.

faq.q: Can you act as our ongoing compliance team?
faq.a: Yes. Our NBFC Compliance Office covers RBI reporting, board and governance support and corporate secretarial compliance on a retainer basis.

faq.q: Which entity should we choose for our startup?
faq.a: Most startups that plan to raise external funding incorporate as a private limited company. We help you weigh the options, including an LLP, based on your plans.

faq.q: What are the annual compliance requirements for a private limited company?
faq.a: Typically board meetings, an annual general meeting, filing financial statements and the annual return with the Registrar of Companies and director KYC, along with event-based filings during the year.

faq.q: Can you help us get Startup India recognition?
faq.a: Yes. We assess eligibility and prepare the application for DPIIT recognition under the Startup India initiative.

faq.q: Can founders based outside India start a company here?
faq.a: Yes, subject to FEMA and FDI rules. Every Indian company needs at least one director who is resident in India, and we can help with this.

faq.q: Do you support startups after they raise funding?
faq.a: Yes. We handle allotment and FEMA filings for the round and continue with ongoing compliance, ESOPs and investor reporting.
